Y7-040.label: Y7-040 · Measure and draw
Y7-040.fact: Measure from the zero on the baseline.
Y7-040.why: Place the centre on the vertex; line up zero with the starting ray.

Y7-041.label: Y7-041 · Lines and angles
Y7-041.fact: Obtuse angles are greater than 90° and less than 180°.
Y7-041.why: This is 125°, not its complementary reading of 55°.

EXT-LEFT.label: Extension · Left-starting angle
EXT-LEFT.fact: Read the scale that begins at the LEFT-hand zero.
EXT-LEFT.why: The starting ray points left. The matching degree scale must start at 0° on the left.

EXT-REFLEX.label: Extension · Reflex angle
EXT-REFLEX.why: A semicircular protractor gives the smaller 120°: 360° − 120° = 240°.

acute.label: Acute · less than a right angle
acute.why: Compare the opening with a right angle, then estimate the part of that quarter turn.

obtuse.label: Obtuse · between 90° and 180°
obtuse.why: A wide angle is more than one quarter turn but less than a half turn.

right.label: Right angle · quarter turn
right.why: A quarter turn is exactly ninety degrees.

straight.label: Straight angle · half turn
straight.why: A half turn forms a straight line: one hundred and eighty degrees.

left.label: Left-starting baseline
left.why: The angle is the opening between rays. Rotating its baseline does not change its size.

reflex.label: Reflex · more than a half turn
reflex.why: The marked direction sweeps past a straight angle. That is more than one hundred and eighty degrees.

gcse.label: GCSE · fine estimation
gcse.why: The opening is just past ninety degrees: estimate the overshoot before measuring.

vertical.label: Y7-041 · Vertically opposite angles

triangle.label: Y7-043 · Angles in triangles
